restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; fresh independent uniform 256-bit words, not seeded PRNG expansion.

Exactly 32-byte messages msg(x)=LE32(x), one chunk with one 64-byte block (zero-filled word loading, true length 32, counter 0, flags CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT); complete unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 1 prefix round and all 256 digest bits.
Single-processor van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point search with theta=2^-32, chain cap L=2^40, budget K0=65300*2^112 evaluations and record cap 2^98; one finite run, no restarts.
One finite run with at most 2^128.3 target-compression equivalents of total charged computation and at most 2^112 peak bytes; no nonuniform advice or precomputed collision.
Analytic resource and success bounds under score-critical heuristic H-RF; no full-scale execution, cryptanalytic weakness or nominal-reference improvement is claimed.

heuristics.statement: Each evaluation of the 1-round BLAKE3 ordinary-collision map f at a fresh input returns a value uniform on {0,1}^256, independent of all previous coins and outputs.
heuristics.scope: Used only for the success-probability bound of the distinguished-point walk (first-contact and bad-event estimates). Correctness and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds hold for every run without this premise.
heuristics.extrapolation: From standard generic-search modeling to the fixed 1-round prefix target; no differential, independence-across-rounds or balance premise about BLAKE3 structure is assumed beyond generic random-function behavior for contact statistics.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is a modeling heuristic, not a proved property of the fixed function. Supporting discussion is analytic (birthday contact arithmetic plus standard DP literature); no organizer-executed scaled experiment is declared. The claimed margin above 0.39 is about 0.0012 before deducting bad events below 7e-10.
